handback.t:
RESEARCH-LEVERS (f4) is done. One new bin, `src/bin/f4_levers.rs`; `src/` is otherwise untouched, with no new crates and no network code. I appended the block "### VERIFY REQUEST — RESEARCH-LEVERS — f4 retrieval/sample-efficiency/critic" to `results/research_board.md`.

Rerun: use the exact command in that block (`CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/Users/mariu/nm-target-hr`, `cargo run --release --offline --bin f4_levers -- --out results/f4_levers.json`). It takes about 4.5 min on 16 cores. Add `--held 61-90 --out results/f4_levers_confirm61-90.json` for the confirmation run, which also takes about 4.5 min. Tuning is on seeds 1-8, held-out 31-60, and the confirmation uses the same frozen tuning on 61-90. Tests are paired 95% t-CI with Holm per family, over 7-10 worlds plus controls in each part.

Everything is measured in my own synthetic world, so none of it says anything about real LLM traffic. No claims of novel knowledge, emergence or "10x".

**(a) Retrieval before routing**
- **Neighbour retrieval is already good once the store is dense.** The `research.rs` default (raw cosine, threshold .6, k5) gets F1 .989 at low noise, .933 for paraphrase, and .594 in a sparse 96-concept world.
- **The tuned configs beat the default in all 9 treatment worlds on both seed sets (Holm).** The gain is +.003 to +.068 F1, and most of it comes from k3 vs k5 rather than centering.
- **Mean-centering matters only in sparse many-concept worlds.** There it adds +.006 (48 concepts) and +.014 (96 concepts) F1 over tuned raw. In dense worlds it is neutral, and it loses early (first 300 queries: -.013 to -.032 at noise 1.2-1.6; Holm LOSS at noise 1.6 on both seed sets).
- **Query expansion helps less than the retune (+.001 to +.023), relative-margin does nothing, and MMR diversity hurts.** MMR is a Holm LOSS in 9 of 9 worlds for raw cosine and 4 of 9 for centered.
- **No single threshold serves both the neighbour list and the anchor vote.** Anchor pair-F1 is only .40 at low noise and .08-.17 in the many-concept worlds. A threshold tuned for the anchors raises it by +.45 but costs -.09 to -.30 neighbour F1.
- **Downstream, the best retriever adds +.027 to +.060 gross quality over warm+reuse without retrieval (Holm WIN).** It adds only +.004 (n.s.) over the default in the main world, and +.017/+.022 in the 48-concept world.
- **Oracle retrieval would add another +.003 (n.s.) at low noise and +.026 to +.032 in the hard worlds.**

**(b) Sample efficiency (graded outcomes until the trailing quality or accuracy target is reached)**
- **Reuse path:** about 330-560 fewer outcomes to quality ≥ .80, Holm WIN in every treatment world on both seed sets. Gross quality gains +.075 to +.129, and it also helps in the irrelevant-notes world, so it is the known reuse effect and not retrieval.
- **Warm start:** gross +.027 to +.047 on 31-60 (WIN in the 5 treatment worlds). On 61-90 it is WIN in 3 of 5 treatment worlds and n.s. in the other two (+.020 to +.024). It is worth 198-355 fewer outcomes in the 48-concept world and in the main world on 61-90 (n.s. on 31-60).
- **Retrieval on top:** 92-164 fewer outcomes. Example in the main world: 196 outcomes with warm+reuse, 89 with the best retriever, 75 with the oracle.
- **Early horizon:** at 250 tasks warm+reuse (.744) is not better than the keyword router (.738), and the cold-start variant is much worse (.620).
- **Censoring:** plain and keyword routing often never reach the target, so the savings are lower bounds.
- **Controls:** the equal-agents world ties on every arm, and the irrelevant-notes world shows no harm or gain from retrieval.

**(c) Generator → critic (31 cells, cost per extra call .01/.03/.10)**
- **The e3 gate does not pay.** At cost .03 it is a Holm net LOSS in 24 of 31 cells on 31-60 (25 on 61-90) and never a WIN. It wins only in a few high-error cells at cost .01.
- **A calibrated trigger pays only in a narrow region.** Checking only when the generator's own confidence is below .3 wins when three things hold: confidence separates bad from good drafts (AUROC ≥ ~.9), at least ~15% of drafts are bad, and a check costs ≤ ~.03.
  - Gains in that region are about +.006 to +.023 net.
  - Example: with 30% base error and AUROC .93, +.0155 on 31-60 and +.0127 on 61-90, both Holm WIN.
  - At AUROC .7-.8, and at cost .10, it never pays. An uninformative confidence is net negative.
- **Retrieval-based triggers (no support, disagreement) do not work.** They catch only 3-15% of bad drafts.
- **Ceiling:** even a trigger that checks exactly the bad drafts gains only about +.03 to +.05, because the checker misses most of them and the retry errs again.
- **Control:** with no errors, every real critic is a small Holm LOSS.

**Caveats and disclosure (full list in the board block)**
- The embeddings, error and note-benefit models, and the self-confidence signal are mine. Real self-confidence AUROC is unknown, so read (c) along the AUROC grid.
- The critic uses the harsh replace-by-retry convention. A verifiable or best-of-two checker was not run and would favour the critic.
- I inspected a first 31-60 run before three fixes: a sign bug in the lower-is-better verdict, an "anchor purity" metric gamed by fragmentation (replaced by pair-F1), and a wider critic grid (new confidence levels, thresholds .1/.2). None of them changed the frozen retrieval choices or the part (b) tables.
- A 61-90 run on an older build was killed unread. The reported 61-90 numbers come from the final build, run once.
